WHAT THE TABLES ARE (my identification). Every header D on this page has the form D = 2p with p prime. The values are 818 (2·409, continued from the previous page), 838 (2·419), 842 (2·421), 862 (2·431), 866 (2·433), 878 (2·439), 886 (2·443), 898 (2·449), 914 (2·457), 922 (2·461) and 926 (2·463). Together with 934 on the next page this is every 2p with p prime from 409 to 467.

The number after D is Gauss's value for the order of the class group of properly primitive positive forms ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 of determinant b^2-ac = -D (discriminant -4D). The next page sorts these D under 'Periodus unica' by number of 'membra', i.e. the class group is cyclic, with one period of h classes.

The table rows. Row 'i.(h-i)' stands for the pair of inverse classes C^i, C^(-i) = C^(h-i), where C is a generator. The last row, i = h/2, is the ambiguous class of order 2, always (2,0,p). That is why its right-hand entry is always 2, and row 0 always has entry 1 for (1,0,D).

- Right column: the first coefficient a of the reduced form in the class C^(±i). When several reduced forms share the same a, the middle coefficient b is added in parentheses. Examples: 926 has 15(2) = (15,2,62) and 15(7) = (15,7,65); 866 has 33(16) = (33,16,34) and 21(10) = (21,10,46). For 886, '10. 89' denotes (10,2,89).
- The rows are successive powers. For 926: C = (3,1,309), C^2 = (9,1,103), C^3 = (27,10,38); then C^4 = (81,-17,15), which reduces to (15,2,62), Gauss's '15(2)'. For 842: C = (29,12,34), C^2 = (3,1,281), C^4 = (9,-2,94), C^6 = (27,7,33).
- Middle column: all representations of D as a sum of three squares, D = x^2+y^2+z^2. Each is written beside one pair of classes. The pairs used are always the alternate rows (all even or all odd), i.e. the classes of one of the two genera. A representation with three distinct nonzero squares corresponds to a pair C^(±i). A representation with a zero or a repeated square corresponds to an ambiguous class: 841+1 sits at row 0, 361+361+144 at row 22 of 866, 576+169+169 at row 18 of 914.
- This is the correspondence of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 291-292. In modern form, r3(D) = 12·h(-4D), with each class of the representing genus accounting for 24 signed ordered representations.

COUNT CHECK (mine), with distinct reps worth 48 and those with a zero or repeated square worth 24:
- 818: 24 + 6·48 + 24 = 336 = 12·28.
- 866: 24 + 10·48 + 24 = 528 = 12·44.
- 878: 5·48 = 240 = 12·20.
- 886: 4·48 + 24 = 12·18.
- 898: 24 + 2·48 + 24 = 12·12.
- 914: 24 + 8·48 + 24 = 12·36.
- 922: 24 + 4·48 = 12·18.
- 926: 10 reps (rows 1,...,19, continued on the next page) give 480 = 12·40.
- 862: 2·48 = 12·8.
- 838: the 3 listed reps plus the omitted 81+81+676 give 168 = 12·14. A direct enumeration of reduced forms of determinant -838 gives a in {1, 2, 7, 11, 14, 19, 22, 23}, i.e. h = 14, matching Gauss's column.

The method, in short: for each D = 2p, Gauss computes the cycle of reduced forms under composition with a generator. He lists all three-square decompositions and attaches them to the classes of the representing genus, cross-checking h against r3(D).
errors: 842: Gauss's class number 22 is wrong; the true value is h(-4·842) = 26 (cyclic, so 'Periodus unica' still holds, but the next page's '22: ...842' is wrong). By enumeration the reduced forms are a = 1, 2 and the pairs a = 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 17, 18, 22, 23, 26, 27, 29. The forms (13,±4,66) and (26,±4,33) are missing. With C = (29,12,34) the true sequence for rows 0..13 is 1, 29, 3, 13, 9, 22, 27, 23, 11, 18, 26, 6, 17, 2. Gauss's 1, 29, 3, 22, 9, 23, 27, 18, [11], 6, 17, 2 is exactly this sequence with 13 (C^3) and 26 (C^10) dropped. Correspondingly the representation 842 = 361+256+225 (19^2+16^2+15^2) is missing: 7 reps give r3 = 24 + 6·48 = 312 = 12·26.
842 row 8: the entry read as '31' (or '71') is impossible, since -842 is not a square mod 31. The correct value is 11 (C^8 = (11,4,78)).
838: the representation 838 = 81+81+676 (9^2+9^2+26^2), belonging to the ambiguous class C^7 = (2,0,419) in the representing genus, is omitted; row 7 is blank. Gauss's h = 14 is nevertheless correct.
926 row 9: the struck-out decomposition 900+25+1 (30^2+5^2+1^2) is correct and is required for the count 10·48 = 12·40. It should not have been cancelled, unless it was rewritten elsewhere.
914 row 4: the correction to 784+121+9 is right (the original was wrong).
922: the class entries for rows 3 and 5 are left blank. By my computation C^3 = (29,±8,34).
Incompleteness only, not an error: 914 gives no class entries on odd rows.

results.what: Tables of the cyclic class groups of binary quadratic forms of determinant -2p (p prime, 409 ≤ p ≤ 463). Each gives the order and the full cycle of reduced forms as powers of a generator, with b noted when several forms share the same a.
results.modern_name: Class group Cl(-8p) computed via Gaussian composition and reduction; tables of class numbers and cyclic structure for imaginary quadratic orders
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (DA 1801; class-number tables in the Nachlass, printed in Werke II)

results.what: Assignment of each representation D = x^2+y^2+z^2 to a pair of inverse classes in one genus, ambiguous classes taking representations with a zero or a repeated square, giving r3(D) = 24·(number of classes in the genus) = 12·h(-4D).
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem, r3(n) = 12 h(-4n) for n ≡ 1,2 mod 4 squarefree

deep.surprise_reason: This is numerical working material for Gauss's known class-number tables and his known theorem linking three-square representations to class numbers. The only noteworthy content is the computational slip for D = 842 (h = 22 instead of 26) and a few omissions.
